faq: Which invoicing tools can you automate?
Xero, QuickBooks Online, FreshBooks, Wave, Zoho Invoice, Stripe invoices and Wix invoices, among others. We confirm what your plan allows before you order.
Will it chase clients without my approval?
Reminders send only in the tone and timing you approve. You can pause them for specific clients, and the Premium package adds an approval step before invoices go out.
Do you set up tax and fee lines on invoices?
We set the tax rates and fees you tell us in the template. You or your accountant must confirm they are right for your location, as we do not give tax advice.
Can invoices be created from a CRM deal?
Yes, in the Premium package. When a deal reaches a stage you choose, a draft invoice is created with the right client and line items for you to check.
desc:
Invoice automation and payment reminders create, send and follow up on invoices from your own accounting or invoicing tool. Ecom Swift LLC sets up the triggers, templates and polite reminders, so billing happens on time without extra typing.

## What is invoice automation?

Invoice automation means your invoicing tool creates and sends invoices from a trigger instead of from a person sitting down to type. The trigger might be a won deal, a completed job, the end of a month or the start of a subscription period. Then the same system sends a reminder before the due date, another when it is overdue, and records the payment when it arrives.

You stay in control. Each invoice can wait for your approval, and nothing changes until you say so.

## Why late invoices mean late cash

Invoicing is easy to postpone. The work is finished, the next job has begun, and the invoice sits on a to-do list for a week. A client who receives a bill late pays late. Chasing unpaid invoices by hand is awkward, so it is often delayed too, and the gap between doing the work and getting paid grows.

Manual billing invites small errors as well: a wrong rate, a missing tax line, an old address or a forgotten recurring client. Each mistake leads to a corrected invoice and a slower payment.

## How automated billing helps cash flow

Sending an invoice promptly sets the payment clock sooner. Reminders before and after the due date keep the invoice in view without a personal message from you each time. Clients tend to respond to a calm, regular prompt, and you avoid the discomfort of writing it yourself.

Recurring invoices are especially well suited. A retainer client receives the same invoice on the same date, with no effort. A status sheet or monthly summary shows what has been sent, paid and overdue, so you can plan with real numbers. Fewer errors also mean fewer disputes.

## What a great invoicing flow includes

- An invoice template with your details, terms and numbering.
- A trigger that creates the invoice, such as a deal won or a date.
- Correct tax, currency and payment terms settings, checked with you.
- A pay link in the email that carries the invoice.
- A copy of each invoice saved to a folder.
- Recurring invoices for clients on a schedule.
- Reminders before and after the due date, in a polite tone.
- An approval step before sending, if you want one.
- A note about late payment added by your own rule.
- A status sheet and a monthly summary of invoices and payments.

## How we set it up

We start with the way you bill today: what triggers an invoice, who receives it, what terms you use and how you want to follow up. We write the rules in plain words and agree on the wording of each reminder, so it matches your voice.

Then we configure your own invoicing or accounting tool, and connect it to a CRM, order source or sheet where needed. We test with draft invoices and sample clients first. Basic sets up one invoice template that is created and sent on a schedule or trigger. Standard adds more templates, recurring invoices, reminders and a status sheet. Premium adds an approval step, late payment wording, creation from CRM or orders, and a monthly summary. We check your tax and currency settings with you, but we are not accountants, so tax rules remain a matter for your own adviser.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Agree your payment terms before building anything.
- Keep reminder messages short, polite and clear.
- Use an approval step until you trust the setup.
- Make sure client billing details are correct in your records.
- Review the status sheet regularly.

**Avoid:**
- Sending automatic reminders to a client with a known dispute.
- Using a harsh tone in the first reminder.
- Changing invoice numbering mid-year without a plan.
- Letting two systems create invoices for the same job.
- Setting up billing before the underlying data is tidy.

## Who it is for

A freelancer or agency with a few retainer clients who wants them billed on the same date every month. A trade or service business that creates an invoice each time a job is marked complete. A small company that sells from a CRM and wants each won deal to produce an invoice without retyping.

## What we need from you

Tell us which invoicing or accounting tool you use, your invoice example, your payment terms and how you want to handle reminders. We work as a collaborator, staff or accountant-style user in your own account where the tool supports it, and we never ask for passwords. You keep full ownership of your records, and any step can wait for your approval.
